newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Email steel plant strike ends.
newsitem.headline: Email steel plant strike ends.

text.p: Australian industrial group Email Ltd said on Tuesday workers at its Martin Bright steel plant have agreed earlier today to return to work after a five-week strike.

Workers at the Martin Bright Steel plant had agreed to accept a nine percent pay increase spread over two years and a one-off payment of A$300 negotiated at a compulsory industrial relations tribunal hearing on Monday.
Martin Bright Steel had been blockaded by picketing workers since April 11. It generates A$70 million of a total A$2.1 billion in group annual sales.

Martin Bright Steel on Monday won Supreme Court injunctions "in respect of the industrial action and had issued writs for damages against the Australian Manufacturing Workers Union (AMWU) and the Australian Workers Union (AWU) and senior officials", Email's group general manager Alan Freer said in a statement.

On top of the pay increase, the steel company agreed to phase in new long service leave entitlements of 13 weeks after 10 years' service by October 2007. This would replace the current allowance after 15 years' long service.
The plant's existing productivity bonus scheme would also be amended to provide a minimum of two percent during the life of the agreement.
"This minimum payment does not represent additional cost to the company as workers have earned well in excess of this amount during the last two years," Freer said.
Freer said PWB Anchor, another company under the Email Metals Group umbrella, had also settled an enterprise agreement with the AMWU and AWU.
PWB Anchor workers agreed to a nine percent pay increase over two years paid in three percent instalments eight months apart and a phased long service leave entitlement, Freer said.
Freer described the settlements as realistic "given the very competitive environment and employee expectations".
Martin Bright Steel workers had asked for a 13 percent wage rise and last week rejected an offer of 8.5 percent.
Thirty percent of Martin Bright Steel's products is exported to the United States, Asia and Europe.
